sections.h2: Why Leland homes can sell fast
sections.html:
Growth defines Leland. The 2025 estimate is 35,731 people, a 52.9% jump from the 23,365 counted in April 2020, and the town had only 13,527 residents in 2010. It sits in Brunswick County.

Newer neighborhoods and a renovated Founders Park give buyers plenty to look at, so an older or worn house needs realistic pricing. Most sellers here weigh a cash sale against an agent listing or a sale handled on their own, and the best fit depends on how much work the house needs and how soon you must move.

Leland skews toward owners and older residents. Owners hold 80.6% of homes. About 28.4% of residents are 65 or older, and only 16.3% are under 18. A midpoint owned home is worth $398,900, rent runs $1,735 at the midpoint, and households earn $91,977 at the midpoint. The town counts 13,219 households, and the average commute is 24.7 minutes.

Owners with a mortgage spend a midpoint of $1,722 a month, and those with no loan $650. A large retiree population means many sellers are weighing a move, a downsize or an estate sale, and buyers often arrive from out of the area. Newer builds and renovated parks set the comparison for your house.

Founders Park at 113 Town Hall Drive reopened after renovation, with an amphitheater and splash pad. The town also tracks the Cape Fear Memorial Bridge replacement project. Buyers who ask about either one can be pointed to the town's website, and you should avoid promising dates for any project.

The Brunswick County Tax Office appraises, bills and collects tax on Leland parcels. Its next countywide revaluation uses values as of January 1, 2027.

All real property is valued on its market value and condition as of that date, and buildings still under construction are valued by percentage complete. Owners should receive notices between February and March 2027 and should compare them with the property record card. The assessor can adjust values in an informal review until the equalization board meets. After that, appeals become formal and are argued before the board. Filing after adjournment is too late for that year, and a changed value reaches forward only.

  • 2026 bills went out in mid-August and stay free of interest until January 5, 2027.
  • Visit the David R. Sandifer Administration Building in Bolivia or call 910-253-2829.
  • The Tax Office can name the rates for your parcel.

Leland's budget for fiscal 2026-2027, which runs from July 1, 2026 to June 30, 2027, totals $50 million, and the town says it reflects a 7.4% reduction in the tax rate.

A buyer weighing two houses will compare total tax bills, and the Tax Office can name the rates for your address. State law sets the due date at September 1 and ties unpaid amounts to the parcel, so a closing office pays any balance from your proceeds.

sections.h2: Tax relief for retirees, heirs and the disabled veteran exclusion
sections.html:
Because Leland has many older residents, state relief programs come up often. Someone who qualifies as a disabled veteran can exclude $45,000 of the permanent residence's appraised value, whatever their age or income. An unmarried surviving spouse might qualify too. The county assessor takes the application.

Filing is due in the listing period, with late filings accepted up to June 1, and circuit breaker applicants refile every year. You may use only one of the three programs, and the assessor can say which suits you.

The home must have been owned and occupied for five years. What the cap defers becomes a lien. When the house is sold or transferred, the latest three years of that deferred tax are owed.

If the owner has died, the clerk of court in the home county can accept a small-estate affidavit covering personal property up to $20,000. Real estate normally takes extra steps, so check with the clerk or an attorney on clearing title before you list.

sections.h2: What buyers ask about a Leland house
sections.html:
Expect questions about the roof, the heating and cooling system and the age of the water heater, along with flood and storm history for the lot. Pull your insurance claims, repair invoices and any permits you have before showings. If you are selling to a cash buyer, those same records help the buyer price the house faster and with fewer discounts.

Ask each buyer how long the title work will take, who orders it, and what happens if something turns up. Compare timelines as well as prices. A slightly lower offer that closes on the date you need can leave you better off than a higher one that drags on, especially if you are carrying a mortgage payment, insurance and the cost of a house that is empty.

Before you accept, confirm the unpaid balance on your loan and any Brunswick County tax owed, and make sure the offer leaves enough to cover both. The closing attorney can run the numbers on a draft settlement statement so nothing changes on closing day.

sections.h2: Which sale method fits a Leland house?
sections.html:
Weigh speed, price and effort. A traditional listing can reward a well-kept house, though you handle showings, repair talks and a buyer's loan timeline. Selling for cash is quicker and takes the house with its flaws, which may lower the price.

  • An agent fits an updated house and a patient owner.
  • Going alone suits a seller who already knows local prices.
  • Cash is useful when damage, put-off repairs, tenants or an estate would slow down a listing.

Keep every offer in writing, learn who covers closing costs and have your attorney check the figures.

sections.h2: Steps to close a Leland sale
sections.html:
1. Start with the newest Brunswick County tax bill and a lender payoff letter.
  2. Line up written offers and see what each leaves in your pocket.
  3. The closing attorney searches title and drafts the settlement statement.
  4. When the house comes through an estate, confirm who may sign the deed before any contract is signed.
  5. Sign at closing. The loan payoff and any unpaid tax are taken from your proceeds first.

With cash there is no loan approval to wait for, so the schedule runs shorter. If the 2027 revaluation notice has not arrived yet, tell buyers a new value is coming, since it may move the tax bill they will see next.

faqs.q: When is Brunswick County's next revaluation?
faqs.a: January 1, 2027 is the effective date, and the county timeline schedules owner notices for February and March 2027.

faqs.q: What is the process to dispute a Brunswick County value?
faqs.a: Request an informal review from the Tax Office, or present a formal appeal after the county's equalization board convenes. If you file once the board has adjourned, the appeal generally waits until next year.

faqs.q: When are Leland property taxes due?
faqs.a: September 1 each year. For 2026 the county says bills are interest-free through January 5, 2027, and that a weekend deadline slides to the next business day.

faqs.q: What does the average Leland house sell for?
faqs.a: The midpoint value for owned homes is $398,900. A particular house varies with age, size, location and condition.

faqs.q: Can a disabled veteran lower a Leland tax bill?
faqs.a: Possibly. For someone who qualifies, $45,000 of the home's appraised value is excluded, and there is no age or income cap. A county Veteran Service Officer fills out the first part, and the form goes to the county assessor.
